chapter_title: Concerning Food: It shall be allocated to Five Products of the human Body.
chapter_note: After a brief hagiographic opening, the chapter is a compact, systematic fivefold teaching: food entering the body is apportioned into five 'productions'. The voice is impersonal and expository, with numbered structure and no NT citation, institutional application, or exhortation—consistent with the older teaching substrate (cosmos/body mechanism rather than church practice).

paragraphs.temporal_note: Formulaic dialogue-frame incipit ('Once again... to his disciples'), characteristic of the compiled Kephalaia hagiographic wrapper.

paragraphs.core_text: This sustenance of various kinds that people gather in and eat, and enters the body; it shall be distributed to five productions.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Impersonal mechanism-statement introducing a numbered fivefold structure; no address, polemic, or institutional mapping.

paragraphs.core_text: The first product is this that shall issue from the person in rapture and rises up in the Mind, and it comes out from all his limbs, and is immeasurable.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Numbered exposition continuing the fivefold schema; body-to-faculty language ('Mind', limbs) presented descriptively rather than hortatively.

paragraphs.core_text: The second is this that shall issue from the person in voice and word.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Plain continuation of the enumerated list; no later markers (no disciples/audience address, no ecclesial application).

paragraphs.core_text: The third is this that shall spring from them in strength and activity.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Still within the closed fivefold production-series; abstract qualities stated as products without moralizing.

paragraphs.core_text: The fourth is what is engendered by the pleasure of lu[s]t in men and women.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Enumerated mechanism statement; despite sexual vocabulary, it remains descriptive (what is engendered) rather than disciplinary command.

paragraphs.core_text: The fifth is this that shall be formed and sculpted in the flesh, and be engendered and come from them. It is this corporeal creature; only its parents can recognise this creature that they beget. They are attentive to its desire and its thought and its [lo]ve every day, all the time. However, these other four forms they neither notice nor are concerned about; because they are not displayed.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Completes the fivefold set and adds an impersonal observational contrast (visible child vs. 'not displayed' productions). No seam into church practice or exhortation; remains within the teaching’s explanatory register.
